problem_identification.critical_issue: Weight cache keyed by raw data_ptr returns stale channels_last filters after allocator reuses the address
evidence: this kernel's output depends on what the CUDA caching allocator previously stored, on shape 8x256x64x128
problem_identification.root_cause: cached_cl() memoises the ChannelsLast weight copy in a global map keyed only by w.data_ptr(), plus sizes/device/version. Freed weight tensors are recycled by the caching allocator, so a new conv1_weight/conv2_weight with different values lands at the same pointer with identical sizes and version 0 -> false cache hit. Both convs then run with the previous run's filter values, changing ~95% of outputs with no NaNs.
problem_identification.trigger_condition: Two runs with fresh weight tensors of the same shape; allocator reuses the freed weight block address, so the stale cached ChannelsLast copy is returned.
must_hold_invariants: Convolution weights used must be derived from the current call's w1/w2 tensor contents
No global cache may be keyed on a recyclable device pointer
Scratch buffers must be fully written before being read
problem_identification.minimal_fix: Delete cached_cl/g_wc and call w1.contiguous(at::MemoryFormat::ChannelsLast) and w2.contiguous(...) per forward, as in the known-good kernel.
